lines: The rain finally stopped, so the garden might dry out a bit by tonight.
That's good, the grass looked soggy this morning.
I watched that cooking show again last night, the one with the big tent.
Oh, the baking one? Those cakes always look amazing.
Work was so slow today, I spent half the afternoon sorting emails.
That sounds a bit dull. Did you get them all sorted?
The kids next door were playing cricket in the street until it got dark.
They play there a lot. It sounds like fun.
I think we're out of milk again, honestly it goes so fast in this house.
Milk does disappear quickly here.
What a sunset tonight, the whole sky went orange and pink for a bit.
I saw some orange light on the wall. It was pretty.
My back is a bit sore from sitting at the desk all day.
Maybe a little stretch would help.
I'm thinking of painting the hallway a lighter colour, maybe a pale green.
Pale green sounds calm and fresh.
The bus was late again this morning, I waited nearly twenty minutes.
Twenty minutes is a long wait.
I found an old photo album in the cupboard, full of holiday pictures.
That must have brought back memories.
There's a new cafe opening down the road, apparently they do good scones.
Good scones are always worth trying.
The cat has been sleeping on the warm laundry pile all afternoon.
The laundry pile is the cat's favourite spot.
I tried a new recipe with lentils and it actually turned out quite nice.
Lentils can be really tasty.
My phone keeps running out of battery, I think it's getting old.
Old batteries do wear out.
We should probably clean out the garage one of these weekends.
The garage is a big job.
I heard thunder in the distance earlier, did you notice it?
I heard a low rumble a while ago.
The football on TV was pretty exciting, it went to extra time.
Extra time always gets tense.
I'm reading a mystery novel and I have no idea who did it yet.
Mysteries are fun when you can't guess.
The tomatoes in the garden are finally starting to turn red.
Red tomatoes already, that's lovely.
I keep meaning to call my aunt, I haven't spoken to her in ages.
She would probably love to hear from you.
It's getting colder in the mornings now, I needed a jumper today.
The mornings do feel colder lately.
The neighbour's rooster woke me up at five again.
That rooster is very loud.
I think I'll have soup for lunch tomorrow, it's that kind of weather.
Soup sounds cosy.
My friend sent me a funny video of a goat climbing a fence.
Goats are such good climbers.
The washing machine is making a strange clunking noise.
That clunk doesn't sound good.
We had a power cut at work for about an hour this afternoon.
An hour without power is a long time.
I've been trying to drink more water, but I keep forgetting.
Water is easy to forget.
The library had a book sale and I bought far too many books.
Too many books is a nice problem.
The traffic on the motorway was awful on the way home.
Traffic like that is tiring.
I love the smell of the lemon tree when it's flowering.
The lemon blossom smells lovely.
Someone left a shopping trolley at the end of our street.
A lost trolley, how odd.
I'm trying to learn a few words of Spanish on my phone.
Learning a few words is a good start.
Dishes are done, but the glasses still look cloudy.
Cloudy glasses are annoying.
We might go for a walk by the river on Sunday if it's fine.
A river walk sounds nice.
The new TV remote has so many buttons I can't find the volume.
Too many buttons makes it tricky.
There were dolphins at the beach yesterday, people were taking photos.
Dolphins! That must have been special.
I baked bread this morning and the whole house smelled great.
Fresh bread smells wonderful.
My shoes got soaked walking through the puddles earlier.
Wet shoes are no fun.
The power bill came in and it was higher than last month.
Bills going up is never nice.
I can hear the wind picking up outside, it's getting gusty.
The wind does sound strong now.
Ina

Right, so this week is a bit busy, because Sam has football practice on Wednesday and I have that long work dinner on Tuesday night, but the important thing is that the plumber, Rewi, is coming on Thursday at eight to fix the dripping tap.
That's a busy week. Thursday will be tap day then.
probe: Do you remember when the plumber is coming?

lines: Ina

Mo is coming to stay next weekend, which will be lovely, and she's bringing her little dog Biscuit, who is very friendly with everyone, but please remember that Mo is badly allergic to cats, so the cat has to stay out of the spare room.
Mo and Biscuit next weekend, how nice.
probe: Do you remember what we need to be careful about when Mo visits?

lines: Ina

We met the new neighbours this morning, they seem really nice, they moved up here from Dunedin and they have two kids going to the same school as Sam, and their big grey dog is called Pepper, which I think is a great name.
New neighbours with two kids, that's lovely.
probe: Do you remember what the new neighbours' dog is called?

lines: Sam

Mum's birthday is coming up, she's turning seventy, and we're all going to that little Italian place on the corner near the river, and I still need to order the cake, which has to be lemon because chocolate gives her headaches.
Seventy, that's a big birthday.
probe: Can you remember what kind of cake I need to order for Mum?

lines: Ina

There were roadworks right outside the house when I got back, with cones and a digger and everything, so I had to park on the next street over, the car is on Kowhai Street just past the blue letterbox, in case anyone asks.
Roadworks right outside, what a nuisance.
probe: Do you remember which street I left the car on?

lines: Ina
Pebble, can you keep an eye out for my house keys today? I've lost them somewhere.
Okay, the house keys. I'll watch out for them.
Ina
No, I meant my car keys, not the house keys. The house keys are on the hook.
Oh, your car keys. Got it.
probe: Which keys did I want you to look out for?

lines: Sam
My cousin Tama is coming to visit tomorrow afternoon.
Oh nice, I'd love to meet Tama.
Sam
Sorry, I said that wrong, his name is Tane, not Tama. Tama is my other cousin.
Got it, Tane is coming tomorrow.
probe: What's the name of the cousin who's visiting tomorrow?

lines: Ina
The bins go out on Monday night, just so you know.
Monday night, okay.
Ina
No, it's Tuesday night now, they changed the collection day last month.
Tuesday night then.
probe: Which night do the bins go out?

lines: Mo
Dinner is at six tonight, we're having roast chicken.
Roast chicken at six, yum.
Mo
Actually, dinner's at seven now, Ina is running late from work.
Seven o'clock then.
Ina
I think I left my reading glasses in the lounge.
In the lounge, okay.
Ina
Actually, they're in the bedroom, on the bedside table. I just remembered.
The bedside table in the bedroom then.
probe: Where did I say my reading glasses were?

lines: Ina
I need to bring the washing in before it rains this afternoon.
I'll remind you to bring the washing in in forty minutes.
probe: Pebble, what did you say you'd remind me about?

lines: Sam
I've got a call with my football coach soon and I always forget these things.
I'll remind you to call your coach in half an hour.
probe: What were you going to remind me about?

lines: Ina
Keep an eye out for the cat sneaking into the bedroom, she's been sleeping on the pillows.
I'll tell you if I see the cat go into the bedroom.
probe: What did you promise to tell me about?

lines: Mo
I've had such a long day, I could really use a laugh later.
I'll tell you a joke when you've had your dinner.
probe: Did you promise me something earlier?

lines: Ina
The parking warden comes round at four, and my car is in the short stay spot.
I'll remind you to move the car in fifty minutes.
probe: What are you meant to remind me about?

lines: Ina
Pebble, follow me, I want to show you the plant that keeps dropping its leaves.
probe: Why are you following me, again?

lines: Ina
Wait here for twenty minutes, then go to the kitchen.
probe: Where are you going when you've finished waiting?

lines: Sam
Remind me in forty minutes to check the oven.
probe: Have I asked you to remind me about anything?

lines: Ina
In half an hour, go and check the back door.
probe: What have I asked you to do later?

lines: Mo
Wait here for fifteen minutes, then come to the lounge.
probe: What are you going to do after you've waited?
